claim: Amphibians and fish have the ability to regenerate numerous tissues, whereas mammals have a limited regenerative capacity.
source: Amphibians and fish have the ability to regenerate numerous tissues, whereas mammals have a limited regenerative capacity.
evidence: This is a general statement presented in the abstract that establishes the comparative regenerative capacities across vertebrate groups.

claim: Numerous developmental genes become reactivated during regeneration.
source: Despite numerous developmental genes becoming reactivated during regeneration, an extensive analysis is yet to be performed on whether highly regenerative animals utilize unique cis-regulatory elements for the reactivation of genes during regeneration and how such cis-regulatory elements become activated.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the abstract, setting up the research question.

claim: Noncoding elements conserved from fish to human function as enhancers in the regenerating nephric tubules.
source: Here, we screened regeneration signal-response enhancers at the lhx1 locus using Xenopus and found that the noncoding elements conserved from fish to human function as enhancers in the regenerating nephric tubules.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the transgenic screening experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: A DNA-binding motif of Arid3a is commonly found in RSREs.
source: A DNA-binding motif of Arid3a, a component of H3K9me3 demethylases, was commonly found in RSREs.
evidence: This finding is based on motif analysis of the identified RSREs as shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Arid3a binds to RSREs and reduces the H3K9me3 levels.
source: Arid3a binds to RSREs and reduces the H3K9me3 levels.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figures 4D and 5C.

claim: Arid3a promotes cell cycle progression and causes the outgrowth of nephric tubules.
source: It promotes cell cycle progression and causes the outgrowth of nephric tubules, whereas the conditional knockdown of arid3a using photo-morpholino inhibits regeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunostaining for phosphorylated histone H3 in Figure 5A and live imaging in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Conditional knockdown of arid3a using photo-morpholino inhibits regeneration.
source: It promotes cell cycle progression and causes the outgrowth of nephric tubules, whereas the conditional knockdown of arid3a using photo-morpholino inhibits regeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the photo-morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Arid3a contributes to the regeneration of nephric tubules by decreasing H3K9me3 on RSREs.
source: These results suggest that Arid3a contributes to the regeneration of nephric tubules by decreasing H3K9me3 on RSREs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined ChIP-qPCR and functional knockdown experiments.

claim: Metanephros is the adult kidney in higher vertebrates, such as humans and mice.
source: Metanephros is the adult kidney in higher vertebrates, such as humans and mice, whereas mesonephros is the adult kidney in fish and amphibians.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge cited with reference to Jones, 2005 and Desgrange and Cereghini, 2015.

claim: Mesonephros is the adult kidney in fish and amphibians.
source: Metanephros is the adult kidney in higher vertebrates, such as humans and mice, whereas mesonephros is the adult kidney in fish and amphibians.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge cited with reference to Jones, 2005 and Desgrange and Cereghini, 2015.

claim: Pronephros is the simplest and earliest kidney form.
source: Pronephros is the simplest and earliest kidney form (Jones, 2005; Desgrange and Cereghini, 2015).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The functional unit of the three kidney types, the nephron, does not differ much.
source: Despite the different levels of complexity of these three kidney types, their functional unit, the nephron, does not differ much (Brändli, 1999; Lienkamp, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In human, there are approximately one million nephrons per kidney.
source: In human, there are approximately one million nephrons per kidney (Saxén and Sariola, 1987).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Each nephron is composed of a glomerulus and a nephric tubule divided into four basic domains: proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, and connecting tubule.
source: Each nephron is composed of a glomerulus, a filtering component, and a nephric tubule, which is divided into the following four basic domains: proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, and connecting tubule (Saxén and Sariola, 1987).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The nephrons of the pronephros in Xenopus laevis can be subdivided into four distinct segments that are homologous to the segments of the metanephric nephrons of mammals.
source: According to molecular studies, the nephrons of the pronephros in Xenopus laevis can be subdivided into four distinct segments that are homologous to the segments of the metanephric nephrons of mammals (Raciti et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on molecular studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: X. laevis is considered a suitable model for studying renal regeneration for application to human.
source: Owing to these similarities, X. laevis is considered a suitable model for studying renal regeneration for application to human.
evidence: This is an inference based on the homology between Xenopus and mammalian nephrons.

claim: Numerous vertebrates have the ability to repair damage to nephric structures, although this regenerative ability diverges between species.
source: Gentamicin-induced nephropathy and partial nephrectomy showed that numerous vertebrates have the ability to repair damage to nephric structures, although this regenerative ability diverges between species (Nonclercq et al., 1992; Diep et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2010; Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: In mammals, nephrons contain mature tubular epithelial cells that have the capacity to regenerate following acute kidney injury.
source: In mammals, nephrons contain mature tubular epithelial cells that have the capacity to regenerate following acute kidney injury (Maeshima et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Tubular epithelial cells rapidly lose their brush border, dedifferentiate into mesenchymal-like cells, and then migrate into regions where cells are damaged.
source: These epithelial cells rapidly lose their brush border, dedifferentiate into mesenchymal-like cells, and then migrate into regions where cells are damaged (Maeshima et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian kidney regeneration supported by citation.

claim: Renal stem cells and progenitor cells were found in the metanephric mesenchyme, limb of Henle's loop, and distal convoluted tubule in mice.
source: Recent cell lineage studies have also suggested that renal stem cells and progenitor cells were found in the metanephric mesenchyme, limb of Henle's loop, and distal convoluted tubule in mice (Kobayashi et al., 2008; Barker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on cell lineage studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The regenerative capacity of mammalian nephrons is restricted to the reconstruction of nephric epithelial cells in damaged regions.
source: Although mammalian nephrons possess cells that contribute to repair after injury, the regenerative capacity is restricted to the reconstruction of nephric epithelial cells in damaged regions (Maeshima et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: X. laevis and zebrafish regenerate fully coiled and functional nephric tubule architecture after severe damage.
source: In contrast to mammals, which merely reconstitute tubular epithelial cells after injury, previous studies showed that X. laevis and zebrafish regenerate fully coiled and functional nephric tubule architecture after severe damage (Diep et al., 2011; Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is based on previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: In zebrafish, the transplantation of lhx1a-positive or six2 mesenchymal cells into adult fish with gentamicin-injured kidneys reconstructs functional nephrons.
source: In zebrafish, the transplantation of lhx1a-positive or six2 mesenchymal cells, which are considered stem cells, into adult fish in which the kidney has been injured by gentamicin reconstructs functional nephrons (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: X. laevis regenerates the functional pronephros that can uptake albumin again after the mechanical loss of proximal tubules.
source: X. laevis also regenerates the functional pronephros that can uptake albumin again after the mechanical loss of proximal tubules (Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: Zebrafish use kidney stem cells to repair the functional nephrons, whereas X. laevis appear to use remaining tubule cells to regenerate the functional pronephros.
source: Zebrafish use kidney stem cells to repair the functional nephrons, whereas X. laevis appear to use remaining tubule cells to regenerate the functional pronephros (Diep et al., 2011; Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is a comparison based on previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Protocols for generating the nephric structure derived from induced pluripotent cells (iPSCs) and embryonic stem (ES) cells have been established by the combined application of the Wnt activator and other signaling factors such as BMP4.
source: Recently, studies have established protocols for generating the nephric structure derived from induced pluripotent cells (iPSCs) and embryonic stem (ES) cells by the combined application of the Wnt activator and other signaling factors such as BMP4 (Xia et al., 2013; Takasato et al., 2014; Takasato et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on recent studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Direct reprogramming from fibroblasts into renal tubular epithelial cells (iRECs) has been successfully achieved using a combination of transcription factors whose expression in the kidney is evolutionarily conserved between mice and Xenopus.
source: In addition, direct reprogramming from fibroblasts into renal tubular epithelial cells, called induced renal tubular epithelial cells (iRECs), has been successfully achieved using a combination of transcription factors whose expression in the kidney is evolutionarily conserved between mice and Xenopus (Kaminski et al., 2016; Lienkamp, 2016).
evidence: This is based on recent studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The molecular mechanisms that allow the reactivation of developmental genes during regeneration in highly regenerative animals remain unclear.
source: However, although the molecular factors for the construction of nephrons in vivo and in vitro have been identified, the molecular mechanisms that allow the reactivation of developmental genes during regeneration in highly regenerative animals remain unclear.
evidence: This is a statement of the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: BMP and canonical Wnt and Fgf signals first specify intermediate mesoderm to form the pronephric primordium, followed by epithelialization, during kidney development.
source: Genetic studies have shown that BMP and canonical Wnt and Fgf signals first specify intermediate mesoderm to form the pronephric primordium, followed by epithelialization, during kidney development (Krause et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from genetic studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Transcription factors such as Osr1, Osr2, Pax8, Hnf1b, Lhx1, and WT1 coordinately regulate kidney formation.
source: In addition to signaling factors, transcription factors such as Osr1, Osr2, Pax8, Hnf1b, Lhx1, and WT1 also coordinately regulate kidney formation (Bouchard, 2004; Lienkamp, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Developmental genes for the kidney are evolutionarily conserved between pronephros formation in Xenopus and the more complex nephrons in mammalian meso- and metanephros.
source: These developmental genes for the kidney are evolutionarily conserved between pronephros formation in Xenopus and the more complex nephrons in mammalian meso- and metanephros (Lienkamp, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: During the regeneration of nephrons in zebrafish, transplanted lhx1a-positive mesenchymal cells begin to express developmental genes such as pax2a, wt1a, and fgf8a.
source: During the regeneration of nephrons in zebrafish, transplanted lhx1a-positive mesenchymal cells begin to express developmental genes such as pax2a, wt1a, and fgf8a (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: Over 43,000 active enhancers have been identified in the human genome.
source: Enhancers are known to determine the tissue specificity and timing of gene expression, and over 43,000 active enhancers have been identified in the human genome alone (Andersson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Numerous enhancers for tissue and organ development have been identified by the deletion mapping of upstream genomic regions and/or candidate screening using the epigenetic landscape.
source: To date, numerous enhancers for tissue and organ development have been identified by the deletion mapping of upstream genomic regions and/or candidate screening using the epigenetic landscape (Kleftogiannis et al., 2016), whereas only a few enhancers for tissue regeneration have been reported, such as tissue regeneration enhancer elements for zebrafish heart reconstruction (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Only a few enhancers for tissue regeneration have been reported, such as tissue regeneration enhancer elements for zebrafish heart reconstruction.
source: To date, numerous enhancers for tissue and organ development have been identified by the deletion mapping of upstream genomic regions and/or candidate screening using the epigenetic landscape (Kleftogiannis et al., 2016), whereas only a few enhancers for tissue regeneration have been reported, such as tissue regeneration enhancer elements for zebrafish heart reconstruction (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The genome of vertebrates contains more enhancers that promote gene expression in regenerating tissues.
source: Although it is generally assumed that the genome of vertebrates contains more enhancers that promote gene expression in regenerating tissues, the difficulty in identifying the in vivo function of enhancers prevents us from revealing the cis-regulatory architecture for regeneration.
evidence: This is a general assumption stated in the manuscript.

claim: An in vivo enhancer mapping system using X. laevis transgenesis has been previously established.
source: We have previously established an in vivo enhancer mapping system using X. laevis transgenesis (Ogino et al., 2008; Ochi et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2015).
evidence: This refers to previous work by the authors cited in the manuscript.

claim: lhx1 expression was induced within 24 hr after the surgical removal of nephric tubules.
source: We first found that lhx1 expression was induced within 24 hr after the surgical removal of nephric tubules.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in situ hybridization experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Genomic elements that are conserved from fish to human, called regeneration signal-response enhancers (RSREs), were activated in regenerating nephric tubules.
source: In order to explore the induction mechanisms of lhx1 in regenerating nephric tubules, we screened enhancers in genomic loci using a transgenic mapping system and found that genomic elements that are conserved from fish to human, called regeneration signal-response enhancers (RSREs), were activated in regenerating nephric tubules.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the transgenic screening shown in Figure 3.

claim: Arid3a is a member of the AT-rich interaction domain family.
source: A putative binding motif of Arid3a, a member of the AT-rich interaction domain family, is commonly found in RSREs for lhx1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the protein family.

claim: Arid3a directly binds to RSREs.
source: We found that Arid3a directly binds to RSREs and Arid3a with H3K9me3 demethylases Kdm4/Jmjd2 reducing H3K9me3 levels on RSREs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Arid3a with H3K9me3 demethylases Kdm4/Jmjd2 reduce H3K9me3 levels on RSREs.
source: We found that Arid3a directly binds to RSREs and Arid3a with H3K9me3 demethylases Kdm4/Jmjd2 reducing H3K9me3 levels on RSREs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Arid3a is required for the regeneration of nephric tubules through the RSREs.
source: We now demonstrate that Arid3a is required for the regeneration of nephric tubules through the RSREs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the conditional knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: The pronephric kidneys of X. laevis become functional from Nieuwkoop and Faber stages 37–38.
source: The pronephric kidneys of X. laevis become functional from Nieuwkoop and Faber stages 37–38.
evidence: This is established developmental knowledge about Xenopus.

claim: Proximal tubules that have been partially nephrectomized at stages 37–38 can regenerate functional nephrons.
source: A previous study showed that proximal tubules that have been partially nephrectomized at stages 37–38 can regenerate functional nephrons (Raciti et al., 2008; Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is based on previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP) transgenic line can be used to trace nephric tubule formation.
source: Since we have previously established the Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP) transgenic line that can be used to trace nephric tubule formation, we first confirmed the regenerative process of nephric tubules using live imaging of stage 37 transgenic embryos (Ochi et al., 2012).
evidence: This refers to a previously established transgenic line cited in the manuscript.

claim: Nephric tubule surgery did not damage the glomus, which is situated medially to the tubules displaying podocin expression.
source: Our careful nephric tubule surgery did not damage the glomus, which is situated medially to the tubules displaying podocin expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization for podocin shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: When the proximal tubules were partially nephrectomized, a coiled structure appeared at around 24 hr.
source: When the proximal tubules were partially nephrectomized, a coiled structure appeared at around 24 hr (Figures 1A, B and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by live imaging shown in Figure 1B and E.

claim: The coiled tubule continued to extend from 24 to 48 hr, and then the regenerated tubules reconstructed the nephron between 72 and 120 hr.
source: This coiled tubule continued to extend from 24 to 48 hr, and then the regenerated tubules reconstructed the nephron between 72 and 120 hr (Figure 1B and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by live imaging shown in Figure 1B and E.

claim: Completely nephrectomized proximal tubules failed to form a coiled structure, whereas the remaining tubules, the intermediate tubules, continued to extend from the back to the front.
source: In contrast, completely nephrectomized proximal tubules failed to form a coiled structure, whereas the remaining tubules, the intermediate tubules, continued to extend from the back to the front (Figure 1C and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by live imaging shown in Figure 1C and E.

claim: When the intermediate tubules were completely removed, no tubule extension was observed.
source: Conversely, when the intermediate tubules were completely removed, no tubule extension was observed (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by live imaging shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: The proximal tubules are essential for the regeneration of the coiled structure of the nephric duct.
source: Thus, although Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP) cannot capture all of the cells that contribute to the reconstruction of nephric tubules, our results indicate that the proximal tubules are essential for the regeneration of the coiled structure of the nephric duct.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: The intermediate tubules have the capacity to regenerate nephric tubules, although this capacity is limited compared with that of the proximal tubules.
source: In addition, the intermediate tubules also have the capacity to regenerate nephric tubules, although this capacity is limited compared with that of the proximal tubules.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Apoptotic cells and the expression of matrix metalloproteinase nine dramatically increase within 12 hr after nephrectomy, and these events continue until 24–48 hr.
source: It has been shown in a previous study that apoptotic cells and the expression of matrix metalloproteinase nine dramatically increase within 12 hr after nephrectomy, and these events continue until 24–48 hr (Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: Regenerative tubules exhibit a coiled structure at around 24–48 hr.
source: Our observation that regenerative tubules exhibit a coiled structure at around 24–48 hr together with previous findings suggests that the genetic mechanisms that occur within 48 hr after nephrectomy are crucial for nephron regeneration.
evidence: This is based on the live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: The genetic mechanisms that occur within 48 hr after nephrectomy are crucial for nephron regeneration.
source: Our observation that regenerative tubules exhibit a coiled structure at around 24–48 hr together with previous findings suggests that the genetic mechanisms that occur within 48 hr after nephrectomy are crucial for nephron regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of coiled structure formation and previous findings.

claim: osr1, osr2, and lhx1, together with pax8, induce ectopic nephrons when overexpressed in Xenopus embryos.
source: Among them, osr1, osr2, and lhx1, together with pax8, are known to induce ectopic nephrons when overexpressed in Xenopus embryos (Seufert et al., 1999; Carroll and Vize, 1999; Tételin and Jones, 2010), and lhx1- or six2-expressing mesenchymal cells can reconstruct functional nephrons in kidney-injured zebrafish (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: lhx1- or six2-expressing mesenchymal cells can reconstruct functional nephrons in kidney-injured zebrafish.
source: Among them, osr1, osr2, and lhx1, together with pax8, are known to induce ectopic nephrons when overexpressed in Xenopus embryos (Seufert et al., 1999; Carroll and Vize, 1999; Tételin and Jones, 2010), and lhx1- or six2-expressing mesenchymal cells can reconstruct functional nephrons in kidney-injured zebrafish (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: The expression of lhx1, pax8, hnf4a, hnf1b, and osr2 appeared within 24 hr after the nephrectomy.
source: The in situ hybridization analysis showed that the expression of lhx1, pax8, hnf4a, hnf1b, and osr2 appeared within 24 hr after the nephrectomy (Figures 2A, D, G and J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figures 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of lhx1, pax8, hnf4a, hnf1b, and osr2 became stronger around 48 hr after nephrectomy.
source: Such expression became stronger around 48 hr (Figures 2B, E, H and K, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figures 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of lhx1 disappeared at 96 hr, while the expression of pax8 was still detected in the nephric tubules.
source: Then, the expression of lhx1 disappeared at 96 hr, while the expression of pax8 was still detected in the nephric tubules (Figures 2C, F, I and L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2.

claim: The expression of pax2 and osr1 appeared around 48 hr after nephrectomy.
source: In contrast, the expression of pax2 and osr1 appeared around 48 hr, and that of six2 was not detected in regenerating nephric tubules (Figure 2M–2R, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, data not shown).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of six2 was not detected in regenerating nephric tubules.
source: In contrast, the expression of pax2 and osr1 appeared around 48 hr, and that of six2 was not detected in regenerating nephric tubules (Figure 2M–2R, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to data not shown.

claim: The immediate induction of lhx1, pax8, hnf4a, hnf1b, and osr2 after nephrectomy suggests that the loci of these genes contain enhancers of injury response.
source: Although it is possible that primary induced lhx1-, pax8-, hnf4a-, hnf1b-, and osr2-expressing cells are not completely consistent with cells observed in Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP) regenerating nephric tubules, the immediate induction of lhx1, pax8, hnf4a, hnf1b, and osr2 after nephrectomy suggests that the loci of these genes contain enhancers of injury response.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of gene expression after nephrectomy.

claim: Lhx1 with Pax8 can induce ectopic pronephron structures.
source: It has been shown in a previous study involving simple mRNA injection using Xenopus embryos that Lhx1 with Pax8 can induce ectopic pronephron structures (Carroll and Vize, 1999).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: Lhx1 is required for the development of nephric tubules in Xenopus.
source: In addition, tissue-specific lhx1 knockout using CRISPR/Cas9 genome engineering clearly showed that Lhx1 is required for the development of nephric tubules in Xenopus (DeLay et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: 20 CNSs conserved between human and fish and 17 CNSs conserved between frog and zebrafish were identified in the lhx1 locus.
source: This analysis identified 20 CNSs conserved between human and fish and 17 CNSs conserved between frog and zebrafish (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on the MultiPipMaker alignment analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CNSs for lhx1 conserved between frog and zebrafish showed enhancer activities.
source: CNSs for lhx1 conserved between frog and zebrafish showed enhancer activities, whereas CNSs conserved among vertebrates showed much stronger enhancer activities (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transgenic reporter assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: CNSs conserved among vertebrates showed much stronger enhancer activities than those conserved only between frog and zebrafish.
source: CNSs for lhx1 conserved between frog and zebrafish showed enhancer activities, whereas CNSs conserved among vertebrates showed much stronger enhancer activities (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transgenic reporter assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: lhx1 is expressed in developing nephrons at the early tailbud stage and specifies the renal progenitor cell field.
source: It is known that lhx1 is expressed in developing nephrons at the early tailbud stage and specifies the renal progenitor cell field (Taira et al., 1994; Carroll et al., 1999; Cirio et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 have enhancer activities in the eyes and somites at the early tailbud stage, while lacking (CNS20 and CNS35) or showing (CNS17) very weak enhancer activities in developing pronephros.
source: The transgenic reporter analysis using early tailbud embryos showed that CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 have enhancer activities in the eyes and somites at this stage, while lacking (CNS20 and CNS35) or showing (CNS17) very weak enhancer activities in developing pronephros, suggesting that these CNSs primarily function after nephrectomy (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transgenic reporter assay shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 primarily function after nephrectomy.
source: The transgenic reporter analysis using early tailbud embryos showed that CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 have enhancer activities in the eyes and somites at this stage, while lacking (CNS20 and CNS35) or showing (CNS17) very weak enhancer activities in developing pronephros, suggesting that these CNSs primarily function after nephrectomy (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential enhancer activities during development versus regeneration.

claim: Enhancers conserved between human and zebrafish regulate the reactivation of developmental genes in regenerating nephric tubules.
source: These results suggest that enhancers conserved between human and zebrafish regulate the reactivation of developmental genes in regenerating nephric tubules.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transgenic reporter assay results.

claim: Transcription motifs for Arid3a and Spib were commonly found in RSREs.
source: The motif analysis showed that transcription motifs for Arid3a and Spib were commonly found in RSREs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on motif analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: arid3a is expressed in the ectoderm of the early neurula and in the epidermis at the late tailbud stage.
source: arid3a is known to be expressed in the ectoderm of the early neurula and in the epidermis at the late tailbud stage, whereas spib is expressed in the anterior ventral blood islands at the neurula stage (Callery et al., 2005; Costa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: spib is expressed in the anterior ventral blood islands at the neurula stage.
source: arid3a is known to be expressed in the ectoderm of the early neurula and in the epidermis at the late tailbud stage, whereas spib is expressed in the anterior ventral blood islands at the neurula stage (Callery et al., 2005; Costa et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: arid3a is expressed in the nephric tubules.
source: We performed an in situ hybridization analysis in order to determine whether these genes are also expressed in the nephric tubules and found that arid3a is expressed there, whereas spib is not (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: spib is not expressed in the nephric tubules.
source: We performed an in situ hybridization analysis in order to determine whether these genes are also expressed in the nephric tubules and found that arid3a is expressed there, whereas spib is not (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Arid3a protein was detected in proximal tubules and also in the glomus and/or nephrocoelom.
source: In addition, we performed immunostaining of Arid3a using Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP), which showed that Arid3a protein was detected in proximal tubules and also in the glomus and/or nephrocoelom (Figure 4B, orange arrows and orange arrowheads, respectively).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 4B.

claim: lhx1 was induced by conditionally induced arid3a in heat-shock-inducible transgenic X. laevis.
source: Therefore, we next examined whether Arid3a regulates the expression of lhx1 in Xenopus and found that lhx1 was induced by conditionally induced arid3a in heat-shock-inducible transgenic X. laevis (Figure 4C) (Wheeler et al., 2000).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization in heat-shock-inducible transgenic X. laevis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Arid3a activates CNS17 and CNS20 enhancer activities.
source: We found that Arid3a activates CNS17 and CNS20 enhancer activities, whereas no activation was observed in the CNS35 reporter (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by luciferase reporter assay shown in Figure 4E.

claim: No activation was observed in the CNS35 reporter by Arid3a.
source: We found that Arid3a activates CNS17 and CNS20 enhancer activities, whereas no activation was observed in the CNS35 reporter (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by luciferase reporter assay shown in Figure 4E.

claim: CNS35 is located in the intron of aatf.
source: Since CNS35 is located in the intron of aatf, it is possible that the activation mechanism of this CNS is different from those of CNS17 and CNS20.
evidence: This is based on the genomic location shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The activation mechanism of CNS35 is possibly different from those of CNS17 and CNS20.
source: Since CNS35 is located in the intron of aatf, it is possible that the activation mechanism of this CNS is different from those of CNS17 and CNS20.
evidence: This is speculation based on the differential response to Arid3a and genomic location.

claim: During tail regeneration in X. laevis, the inhibition of apoptosis results in a failure to induce subsequent cell proliferation.
source: During tail regeneration in X. laevis, the inhibition of apoptosis results in a failure to induce subsequent cell proliferation (Tseng et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: During proximal tubule regeneration, apoptosis occurs within 3 hr after nephrectomy, and the number of apoptotic cells is decreased at one day.
source: During proximal tubule regeneration, apoptosis occurs within 3 hr after nephrectomy, and the number of apoptotic cells is decreased at one day (Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: There was no significant difference in the number of proliferating cells between the control and the nephrectomized sides until 6 hr after nephrectomy.
source: Immunofluorescence staining with anti-phosphorylated histone H3 antibody, a marker for mitotic cells, showed that there was no significant difference between the control and the nephrectomized sides until 6 hr after nephrectomy, whereas the number of proliferating cells increased on the nephrectomized side at 24 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of proliferating cells increased on the nephrectomized side at 24 hr after nephrectomy.
source: Immunofluorescence staining with anti-phosphorylated histone H3 antibody, a marker for mitotic cells, showed that there was no significant difference between the control and the nephrectomized sides until 6 hr after nephrectomy, whereas the number of proliferating cells increased on the nephrectomized side at 24 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Arid3a stimulates cyclin E1/E2F-dependent cell cycle progression.
source: It has been shown in a previous study that Arid3a stimulates cyclin E1/E2F-dependent cell cycle progression (Peeper et al., 2002).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: The number of phosphorylated histones H3 in the mCherry-positive Xla.Tg(Xla.hsp70:Xtr.arid3a-2A-mcherry, Xtr.pax8:EGFP) was significantly increased compared with controls.
source: In contrast, the number of phosphorylated histones H3 in the mCherry-positive Xla.Tg(Xla.hsp70:Xtr.arid3a-2A-mcherry, Xtr.pax8:EGFP) was significantly increased compared with that in the heat-shock-treated Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP) and heat-shock-untreated Xla.Tg(Xla.hsp70:Xtr.arid3a-2A-mcherry, Xtr.pax8:EGFP) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Transgenic X. laevis in which lhx1 was conditionally induced showed an increased number of phosphorylated histones H3.
source: Transgenic X. laevis in which lhx1 was conditionally induced showed an increased number of phosphorylated histones H3, as observed in Arid3a-induced X. laevis (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Arid3a and Lhx1 promote cell cycle progression after nephrectomy.
source: These results suggest that Arid3a and also Lhx1 promote cell cycle progression after nephrectomy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunostaining experiments shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: The constitutive heterochromatin marker histone 3 lysine nine trimethylation (H3K9me3) is rapidly remodeled to create a chromatin environment.
source: The constitutive heterochromatin marker histone 3 lysine nine trimethylation (H3K9me3) is rapidly remodeled to create a chromatin environment, and the lack of H3K9me2/3 could allow global DNA demethylation (Burton and Torres-Padilla, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Arid3a stimulates the expression of immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgH) and changes the accessibility of the IgH enhancer.
source: Arid3a is known to stimulate the expression of immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgH) and is also known to change the accessibility of the IgH enhancer (Kim and Tucker, 2006; Lin et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The complex of Arid3a, Arid3b, and Kdm4c modulates the chromatin configuration of stemness genes for breast cancer by decreasing H3K9me3.
source: In addition, it has been shown in a previous study that the complex of Arid3a, Arid3b, and Kdm4c modulates the chromatin configuration of stemness genes for breast cancer by decreasing H3K9me3 (Liao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: H3K9me3 was enriched on the RSREs CNS17 and CNS20, as well as on CNS32 and exon 5 of lhx1.
source: ChIP-qPCR analysis using anti-H3K9me3 showed that H3K9me3 was enriched not only on the RSREs CNS17 and CNS20, but also on CNS32 and exon 5 of lhx1 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 5C.

claim: No enrichment of H3K9me3 on CNS35 was observed.
source: However, no enrichment of H3K9me3 on CNS35 was observed (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The coinjection of arid3a, arid3b, and kdm4a decreased H3K9me3 on the RSREs CNS17 and CNS20, but not on CNS32.
source: Next, we found that the coinjection of arid3a, arid3b, and kdm4a decreased H3K9me3 on the RSREs CNS17 and CNS20, but not on CNS32 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The enrichment of H3K9me3 on exon 5 was decreased by the coinjection of arid3a, arid3b, and kdm4a.
source: In addition, the enrichment of H3K9me3 on exon 5 was also decreased (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Arid3a directly regulates lhx1 expression through changing the chromatin configuration on CNS17 and CNS20.
source: Thus, we found that Arid3a directly regulates lhx1 expression through changing the chromatin configuration on CNS17 and CNS20.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Both the chromatin modification and the activation mechanism of CNS35 differ from those of CNS17 and CNS20.
source: In contrast, although CNS35 shows an enhancer activity in regenerating nephric tubules, both the chromatin modification and the activation mechanism differ from those of CNS17 and CNS20.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential responses observed in the ChIP-qPCR and luciferase assays.

claim: The arid3a.L-MO-injected embryos became abnormal during gastrulation.
source: The arid3a.L-MO-injected embryos became abnormal during gastrulation, consistent with the phenotype that was previously reported using translational blocking morpholino (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) (Callery et al., 2005).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the morpholino injection experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The level of transcripts that included exon three was dramatically reduced in arid3a.L-MO-injected embryos.
source: RT-PCR analysis using control and arid3a.L-MO-injected embryos showed that the level of transcripts that included exon three was dramatically reduced in arid3a.L-MO-injected embryos (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-PCR shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Embryos injected with arid3a.L-MO annealed with arid3a.L-Photo-MO developed normally.
source: In contrast, embryos injected with arid3a.L-MO annealed with arid3a.L-Photo-MO developed normally (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the photo-morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: arid3a.L-MO is rendered inactive by binding to arid3a.L-Photo-MO.
source: Thus, arid3a.L-MO is rendered inactive by binding to arid3a.L-Photo-MO.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that embryos develop normally when MO is annealed with Photo-MO.

claim: The arid3a.L transcript, which included exon 3, was significantly decreased by treatment with UV light.
source: RT-PCR analysis showed that the arid3a.L transcript, which included exon 3, was significantly decreased by treatment with UV light, same as upon injection of arid3a.L-MO alone (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RT-PCR shown in Figure 6A.

claim: There was no significant increase of lhx1 in UV-treated embryos after nephrectomy.
source: In situ hybridization analyses showed that there was no significant increase of lhx1 in UV-treated embryos, suggesting that Arid3a is essential for the expression of lhx1 after nephrectomy (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Arid3a is essential for the expression of lhx1 after nephrectomy.
source: In situ hybridization analyses showed that there was no significant increase of lhx1 in UV-treated embryos, suggesting that Arid3a is essential for the expression of lhx1 after nephrectomy (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in situ hybridization experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The number of phosphorylated histone H3-positive cells after nephrectomy in UV-treated embryos was reduced.
source: Therefore, we also examined whether arid3a knockdown induced by UV affects the cell cycle and found that the number of phosphorylated histone H3-positive cells after nephrectomy in UV-treated embryos was reduced (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunostaining shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Most of the resected X. laevis with UV-treated arid3a.L-photo-MO/arid3a.L-MO failed to reconstruct the coiled structure.
source: In contrast, although regenerating proximal tubules extended to the front most of the resected X. laevis failed to reconstruct the coiled structure, indicating that Arid3a is required for the proper regeneration of nephric ducts in X. laevis (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by live imaging shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Arid3a is required for the proper regeneration of nephric ducts in X. laevis.
source: In contrast, although regenerating proximal tubules extended to the front most of the resected X. laevis failed to reconstruct the coiled structure, indicating that Arid3a is required for the proper regeneration of nephric ducts in X. laevis (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the photo-morpholino knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: In many cases of tissue regeneration, numerous developmental genes that are evolutionarily conserved among vertebrates become reactivated during regeneration.
source: In many cases of tissue regeneration, numerous developmental genes that are evolutionarily conserved among vertebrates become reactivated during regeneration (Poss, 2010; Witman et al., 2011; Halasi et al., 2012; Shibata et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: It has been widely discussed that regeneration recapitulates developmental guidance.
source: Therefore, it has been widely discussed that regeneration recapitulates developmental guidance (Witman et al., 2011; Halasi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Tissue regeneration enhancer elements were identified on the basis of epigenetic profiling.
source: Previously, tissue regeneration enhancer elements were identified on the basis of epigenetic profiling (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: RSREs for lhx1 are evolutionarily conserved between human and fish.
source: Here, our transgenic analysis of functional cis-regulatory elements showed that RSREs for lhx1 are evolutionarily conserved between human and fish, and Arid3a with Arid3b and Kdm4a induces lhx1 by changing the chromatin configuration of RSREs (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transgenic screening and ChIP-qPCR experiments.

claim: Knockdown of arid3a causes the failure of regeneration.
source: In addition, we showed that knockdown of arid3a causes the failure of regeneration, whereas the conditionally induced Arid3a promotes cell cycle progression and causes the outgrowth of nephric tubules (Figure 7B and C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the photo-morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6C and Figure 7B.

claim: Conditionally induced Arid3a promotes cell cycle progression and causes the outgrowth of nephric tubules.
source: In addition, we showed that knockdown of arid3a causes the failure of regeneration, whereas the conditionally induced Arid3a promotes cell cycle progression and causes the outgrowth of nephric tubules (Figure 7B and C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the heat-shock-inducible transgenic experiments shown in Figures 5A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: lhx1 is one of the earliest genes to be expressed in the pronephric anlagen, and its expression disappears during proximal tubule development.
source: lhx1 is one of the earliest genes to be expressed in the pronephric anlagen, and its expression disappears during proximal tubule development (Carroll et al., 1999; Carroll and Vize, 1999) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: lhx1 expression appeared at the early stage in the construction of kidneys in vivo.
source: As it recapitulates the developmental program, lhx1 expression appeared at the early stage in the construction of kidneys in vivo (Takasato et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: During in vivo nephric regeneration, lhx1 is one of the earliest genes to be expressed in regenerating nephrons.
source: During in vivo nephric regeneration, lhx1 is one of the earliest genes to be expressed in regenerating nephrons (Figure 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Xenopus lhx1/xlim-1 enhancer responding to activin has been reported to encompass approximately 14.2 kb, including 5 kb upstream and the gene body.
source: The Xenopus lhx1/xlim-1 enhancer responding to activin has been reported to encompass approximately 14.2 kb, including 5 kb upstream and the gene body (Rebbert and Dawid, 1997; Watanabe et al., 2002).
evidence: This is based on previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Enhancers are located not only near the gene body but also far away from it.
source: Since recent genome-wide analyses have shown that enhancers are located not only near the gene body but also far away from it, we compared the genomic sequence of a 365 kb segment encompassing the human LHX1 gene with the orthologous intervals in mice, opossums, X. tropicalis, and zebrafish (Woolfe et al., 2005; Ochi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The activin-responding lhx1 enhancer is located in intron 1.
source: While the activin-responding lhx1 enhancer is located in intron 1, enhancers that showed high activities in regenerating nephrons are located 177 kbp (CNS17) and 144 kbp (CNS20) upstream of lhx1 and are also found in the intron of the next gene aatf (CNS35) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on the genomic location shown in Figure 3.

claim: Enhancers that showed high activities in regenerating nephrons are located 177 kbp (CNS17) and 144 kbp (CNS20) upstream of lhx1 and in the intron of aatf (CNS35).
source: While the activin-responding lhx1 enhancer is located in intron 1, enhancers that showed high activities in regenerating nephrons are located 177 kbp (CNS17) and 144 kbp (CNS20) upstream of lhx1 and are also found in the intron of the next gene aatf (CNS35) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on the genomic location shown in Figure 3.

claim: Many genes have multiple enhancers.
source: It is known that many genes have multiple enhancers (Bulger and Groudine, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Multiple enhancers often play different functional roles, while they sometimes show overlapping functions.
source: Such multiple enhancers often play different functional roles, while it is also known that they sometimes show overlapping functions (Osterwalder et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 are activated in regenerating nephric tubules, indicating that these enhancers have overlapping functions.
source: CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 are activated in regenerating nephric tubules, indicating that these enhancers have overlapping functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transgenic reporter assay results.

claim: CNS17 and CNS20 are modified by H3K9me3 but not CNS35.
source: On the other hand, we also found that CNS17 and CNS20 are modified by H3K9me3 but not CNS35 (Figures 3C and 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Functionally redundant enhancers provide phenotypic robustness.
source: It has been shown in recent studies that functionally redundant enhancers provide phenotypic robustness (Osterwalder et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: There is a redundancy of cis-regulatory elements for regeneration.
source: Our observation that there are overlapping functions of CNS17, CNS20, and CNS35 in the regenerating nephric tubules, albeit with differential activation mechanisms, suggests that there is a redundancy of cis-regulatory elements for regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the overlapping functions of multiple enhancers.

claim: Many CNSs that are only conserved between frog and fish showed weak enhancer activities in regenerating nephric tubules.
source: In addition, we also found that many CNSs that are only conserved between frog and fish showed weak enhancer activities in regenerating nephric tubules (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transgenic reporter assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Weak multiple enhancers possessing overlapping activities may be key to boosting the gene expression in regenerating tissues.
source: Since these animals have a high regenerative capacity, it is possible that such weak multiple enhancers possessing overlapping activities may also be key to boosting the gene expression in regenerating tissues.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of weak enhancer activities in frog/fish CNSs.

claim: In zebrafish, lhx1a and six2 mesenchymal cells reconstruct the functional nephrons.
source: In zebrafish, lhx1a and six2 mesenchymal cells reconstruct the functional nephrons (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: The wound healing and regrowth of existing tubules occur during the regeneration of the nephric tubules of X. laevis.
source: In contrast, our live imaging using Xla.Tg(Xtr.pax8:EGFP) together with McLaughlin's previous findings suggests that the wound healing and regrowth of existing tubules occur during the regeneration of the nephric tubules of X. laevis, since the remaining nephric tubule cells extend toward the glomus (Caine and Mclaughlin, 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from live imaging and previous findings.

claim: In mammals, mature tubular epithelial cells rapidly lose their brush border and dedifferentiate into mesenchymal-like cells following acute kidney injury, and these cells proliferate to regenerating nephric tubules.
source: In mammals, mature tubular epithelial cells rapidly lose their brush border and dedifferentiate into mesenchymal-like cells following acute kidney injury, and these cells proliferate to regenerating nephric tubules (Maeshima et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The regenerative mechanisms of the nephric tubules of X. laevis appear to be much closer to the regeneration of nephric tubules in mammals rather than the reconstruction of nephrons from stem cells.
source: Therefore, the regenerative mechanisms of the nephric tubules of X. laevis appear to be much closer to the regeneration of nephric tubules in mammals rather than the reconstruction of nephrons from stem cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the regenerative mechanisms across species.

claim: In vivo organ construction technologies enabled the creation of nephric structures derived from iPSCs and ES cells by the combined application of the Wnt activator and other signaling factors such as BMP4.
source: Recently developed in vivo organ construction technologies enabled us to make nephric structures derived from iPSCs and ES cells by the combined application of the Wnt activator and other signaling factors such as BMP4 (Xia et al., 2013; Takasato et al., 2014; Takasato et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on recent studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Direct reprogramming from fibroblasts into renal tubular epithelial cells (iRECs) has successfully converted mouse and human fibroblasts into renal tubular epithelial cells using a combination of transcription factors: Emx2, Hnf1b, Hnf4a, and Pax8.
source: Moreover, direct reprogramming from fibroblasts into renal tubular epithelial cells, called iRECs, has successfully converted mouse and human fibroblasts into renal tubular epithelial cells using a combination of transcription factors: Emx2, Hnf1b, Hnf4a, and Pax8 (Kaminski et al., 2016; Lienkamp, 2016).
evidence: This is based on recent studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: mRNA injection of Wnt11b, Osr1, Osr2, and Lhx1 with Pax8 can induce ectopic pronephron structures in Xenopus.
source: In Xenopus, it is well known that mRNA injection of Wnt11b, Osr1, Osr2, and Lhx1 with Pax8 can induce ectopic pronephron structures (Seufert et al., 1999; Carroll and Vize, 1999; Tételin and Jones, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Arid3a is not strong enough to induce complete ectopic nephrons as with Osr1, Osr2, Lhx1, and Pax8 mRNA injection.
source: Although Arid3a is not strong enough to induce complete ectopic nephrons as with Osr1, Osr2, Lhx1, and Pax8 mRNA injection, our findings suggest that Arid3a may contribute to the improvement of the efficiency of in vitro reconstruction and in vivo direct reprogramming or regeneration of nephrons.
evidence: This is a comparison based on the experimental results.

claim: Arid3a may contribute to the improvement of the efficiency of in vitro reconstruction and in vivo direct reprogramming or regeneration of nephrons.
source: Although Arid3a is not strong enough to induce complete ectopic nephrons as with Osr1, Osr2, Lhx1, and Pax8 mRNA injection, our findings suggest that Arid3a may contribute to the improvement of the efficiency of in vitro reconstruction and in vivo direct reprogramming or regeneration of nephrons.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study.

claim: Arid3a changes its localization from cytoplasmic to nuclear, which is regulated by importin-9.
source: For the expression of stem cell factors, Arid3a changes its localization from cytoplasmic to nuclear, which is regulated by importin-9 (Liao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: A disintegrin and metalloproteinase 13 (ADAM13) increases the nuclear localization of a cleavage product of Arid3a and promotes the expression of the target gene tfap2 alpha.
source: It has been shown in a recent study that A disintegrin and metalloproteinase 13 (ADAM13) increases the nuclear localization of a cleavage product of Arid3a and promotes the expression of the target gene tfap2 alpha (Khedgikar et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on a recent study cited in the manuscript.

claim: ADAMs control a variety of cell functions by modulating the ectodomain shedding of several membrane-anchored signaling molecules.
source: ADAMs are known to control a variety of cell functions by modulating the ectodomain shedding of several membrane-anchored signaling molecules (Blobel, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: ADAMs are required for wound healing and the regeneration of oligodendrocytes.
source: In addition, emerging evidence indicates that ADAMs are required for wound healing and the regeneration of oligodendrocytes (Schönefuß et al., 2012; Palazuelos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ADAMs may change the localization of Arid3a after nephrectomy; nuclear-translocated Arid3a regulates H3K9me3 on RSREs, and this epigenetic alteration triggers lhx1 expression in regenerating nephric tubules.
source: Therefore, it is possible that ADAMs change the localization of Arid3a after nephrectomy; nuclear-translocated Arid3a regulates H3K9me3 on RSREs, and this epigenetic alteration triggers lhx1 expression in regenerating nephric tubules.
evidence: This is speculation based on the known functions of ADAMs and Arid3a.
